challenges.says: The Apply/OK/Cancel reporting, the list-refresh and 'nothing written until Save Policies' criteria (rules 53979609, 37207468, 65724709, 07359577, 75178338) and the 'forgotten first, then written' save criterion (84933301, 33456476) are about saving and closing, not opening, so they sit in the wrong story and duplicate what the 'Save the policy and carry on or finish' story promises.

Several criteria bundle two or three unrelated rules with 'Also:' (supported-on text with state shown, reading choice with check box, list reading with the 'every value present' check), which makes them hard for a product owner to test as one criterion, and 'whole value list' and 'first item whose own value' are builder wording not owner wording.

The number-box criterion drops rule 76178080's conditions that only typing is restricted to digits (pasted text is not) and that a negative number kept where the minimum is below zero is converted to an unsigned number when applied, and the unnamed-list criterion drops that a row whose value cell was never filled is returned as an empty entry; the open questions only partly cover these.

No rule states a forecast: every criterion restates a write-time rule of the state writer as 'when the forecast is shown, then ... is listed', which invents a forecast listing the rules do not describe, while the open question admits its layout and confirmation are undecided.

The criterion for Enabled combines rule 60774486 (every option is written, including options never filled in) with rule 97175686 (only supplied settings are written, an unsupplied one is left as it was) into one sentence that reads as self-contradictory, and the conflict between the two rules is neither resolved nor flagged.

The REG file and policy file criteria use words a product owner would not follow ('key's clearance is forgotten', 'key-removal entry', 'clear-all marker', 'source branch') and describe storage internals rather than what the person sees.

The story's what and why speak of confirming the forecast and of OK, Apply and closing, but none of its criteria says any of that, because they are all registry-writing rules of the option value writer (and rule 80911529's 'delete' value), so the criteria do not match the title and a story about carrying on or finishing has no criterion on carrying on or finishing.

Criteria use technical wording a product owner could not follow ('32-bit number', 'expandable string', 'multiple-string value', 'defined as delete', 'extra values', 'registry key') without saying what the person gets.
